title: Government Shutdown: Explained — opening chapter
sources: Congressional Research Service, 'Shutdown of the Federal Government: Causes, Processes, and Effects' (RL34680): appropriations lapse at the start of the fiscal year on October 1 without enacted funding
US Office of Personnel Management guidance on furloughs and excepted (essential) employees during a lapse in appropriations
AP and Reuters reporting on federal shutdowns: hundreds of thousands of employees furloughed, others required to work without pay until funding is restored

lines.text: On October first, the government ran out of money.
lines.caps: On *October first, | the government | ran out of *money.

lines.text: Not all of it. Just the parts Congress hadn't funded.
lines.caps: Not *all of it. | Just the parts | Congress *hadn't funded.

lines.text: So hundreds of thousands of federal workers were sent home.
lines.caps: *Hundreds of thousands | of federal workers | were sent *home.

lines.text: Or told to keep working, for no pay.
lines.caps: Or told to | keep *working, | for *no pay.

lines.text: And every day it lasted, the bill grew.
